Leave granted.

Heard learned Counsel for the parties.
3. Rule.

Respondent No.2 waives notice on behalf of herself.

sentences.text: By this petition, preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the petitioners seek quashing of the FIR bearing C.R. No. 111 of 2020 registered with the Indira Nagar Police Station, Nashik, for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A, 406 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code and consequently the proceeding pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Court Room No.3, Nashik.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Quashing is sought on the premise that the parties have amicably settled their dispute.
5. Perused the papers.
The petitioner No.1 is the husband of the respondent No.2 and the petitioner No.2 is the mother-in-law of the respondent No.2.
It appears that the petitioner No.1 and the 906. wpst 19285-2022.doc respondent No.2 got married on 17 th December, 2008 and from the said marriage have a son aged 13 years, as of today.
As according to the respondent No.2, she has allegedly ill-treated and harassed by the petitioners, she lodged the aforesaid FIR as against the petitioners alleging the aforesaid offences.
After investigtaion, chargesheet was filed and the case is presently pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Court Room No.3, Nashik.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Court Room No.3, Nashik
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. In the interregnum, during the pendency of the aforesaid proceeding, the parties amicably settled their dispute and decided to put a quietus to the same.
No Consent Terms have been filed by the parties.

We are informed that the parties i.e. the petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.2 have filed a petition in the Family Court, Nashik seeking dissolution of their marriage under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act.
7. Learned Counsel for the respondent No.2 has tendered an affidavit of the respondent No.2 dated 14 th December, 2022, duly 906.
wpst 19285-2022.doc affirmed before the Assistant Registrar, High Court.

To the said affidavit,
is annexed a photocopy of the Aadhar Card of the respondent No.2, duly signed by her.

In the said affidavit, the respondent No.2 has in para 3 & 4 stated as under:
"3. I state that I have realized that the said FIR registered out of misunderstanding.

As stated in the petition, the petitioner No.1 husband (Dinesh) and myself have decided to dissolve the marriage by mutual consent u/s 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act in view of the amicable settlement between ourselves.

Accordingly, the petition has been filed in the Family Court at Nashik Road, Nashik along with the consent terms filed therein registered on 26/11/2022 bearing Petition No. F/716/2022 and the same is due further for consideration on 21/2/2023.

entities.text: Family Court at Nashik Road, Nashik
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the consent terms, the interest of the child namely "Amulya" aged 13 years has been considered whereby the petitioner No.1 has waived off his equal right in the flat at Nashik in his favour.

4. As such, the matter has been settled amicably and one of the pre-condition to co-operate the petitioners for quashing of the FIR in the said crime, I hereby given my consent and no objection to quash and set aside the FIR in question i.e. Crime No.
111 of 2020 registered with Indira Nagar Police Station, Nashik on 17/3/2020 u/s 398A, 406, 34 of Indian Penal Code as against the present petitioners.

The same may Dinesh Kushabhau Mandlik And Anr vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122362256/
2 accordingly quash and set aside on consent.

sentences.text:
To continue such proceedings in view of the above development would amount to abuse of process of court."
8.

As we were of the view, that the interest of the child had 906. wpst 19285-2022.doc not been taken into consideration, we asked the petitioner No.1 to contribute 50% of the tuition fees of the child, till the child completes his graduation.
The petitioner No.1 has agreed to the same.
Pursuant thereto, the petitioner No.1 has tendered his affidavit-cum- undertaking dated 15th February, 2023, duly affirmed before the Assistant Registrar, High Court.

In the said affidavit-cum-undertaking of the petitioner No.1 in para 2 to 5 has stated as under;
"2. The son is studying in 7th std.
In the School namely St. Lawrence High School, at Borivali (West), Mumbai.
The payment of annual school fees as on date is Rs.45,000/- for the academic year.
The same needs to be paid in two installments.

3. In undertake to pay 50% of the annual school fees (as second installment) of the son for every academic year directly to the school until his completion of High School education as well as undertake to pay 50% of the college fees (as second installment or part fees as per the scheduled) to be paid for High Education directly to the concerned college until completion of his graduation studies.
4. I further undertake that I will pay 50% of the annual school fees/college fees as per the revise scheduled if any for the respective further years.

5. The undertaking herein filed on the record of the file in the caption matter and I further undertake to comply the same as an statement made to this Hon'ble Court by way of Undertaking."
906.
The petitioner No.1 is present in person.
He undertakes to comply and abide by his undertaking with respect to the payment of 50% school/college fees, directly to the said school/college, well in time.
The said undertaking is accepted as an undertaking to this Court.
10. The respondent No.2 is present in person.
On questioning, she re-iterates what is stated by her in her affidavit.
The respondent No.2 has been identified by the learned Counsel for the petitioners.
A photocopy of her Aadhar Card is annexed to the affidavit filed by the respondent No.2.
The same is duly attested by her and the learned APP has verified the original Aadhar Card of the respondent No.2.

11. Considering the nature of dispute, the relations between the parties, the amicable settlement between them, the affidavit of the respondent No.2, the affidavit-cum-undertaking of the petitioner No.1 and the judicial pronouncements of the Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr.1 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State 1 (2012) 10 SCC 303 Dinesh Kushabhau Mandlik And Anr vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122362256/
3 906. wpst 19285-2022.doc of Punjab & Anr.2, , there is no impediment in allowing the petition.
